This page shows every active MLS® listing for condos in Chilliwack, BC. Here is how the local sub-areas compare.
Downtown Chilliwack (District 1881)
Downtown Chilliwack (District 1881): District 1881 and the downtown core, where most of the city's new mid-rise condos are going up.
Sardis East Vedder
Sardis East Vedder: established family streets east of Vedder Road close to shops, parks and Sardis Secondary.
Garrison Crossing
Garrison Crossing: the former CFB Chilliwack base, now a walkable village of heritage-style homes, townhomes and condos.
Vedder Crossing
Vedder Crossing: the commercial heart of the south side, with condos and townhomes close to the Vedder River.
Chilliwack Proper West
Chilliwack Proper West: entry-level condos and townhomes near Highway 1 and Luckakuck/Young Road.
Sardis South
Sardis South: newer subdivisions and townhome sites toward the Vedder River and Cultus Lake Road.

A condo falls under the BC Strata Property Act as a strata title, which leaves some paperwork to get hold of before you remove subjects. That means the Form B, the depreciation report, the strata minutes for the last two years, and the bylaws that cover rentals, pets and age restrictions. If the complex is 55+ or 45+, at least one occupant must meet its age bylaws.

Parts of Rosedale, Yarrow, Greendale, Fairfield Island and the lower part of Sardis are on the Fraser and Vedder River floodplain, and the City's dike network protects those areas. Ask for the flood construction level of the property, and check lender and insurer requirements too. Also find out whether a covenant, geotechnical or floodplain, is registered on title.

Schools and transit in Chilliwack: the district is School District 33 (SD33), which takes in Sardis Secondary and Chilliwack Secondary as well as G.W. Graham Middle-Secondary, with elementary catchments that include Unsworth, Watson and Vedder. Before buying, have SD33 confirm the catchment. On buses, BC Transit serves Young Road, and also Luckakuck Way and Vedder Road. Route 66, the Fraser Valley Express, runs out of Chilliwack to Abbotsford and over to Carvolth Exchange in Langley.

Where are condos for sale in Chilliwack usually located?

Most condos in Chilliwack come up in Downtown Chilliwack (District 1881), Sardis East Vedder, Garrison Crossing, Vedder Crossing, Chilliwack Proper West and Sardis South. Each area has its own mix of age, lot size and price, so I recommend shortlisting two or three neighbourhoods before you book showings.
How often do these Chilliwack condo listings update?
MLS® listings supplied by the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board sync to this page multiple times each day, so price changes, new listings and sold statuses turn up fast.
What should I check on zoning, strata or ALR before buying a Chilliwack condo?

A condo in BC is owned as a strata title and falls under the Strata Property Act. Ahead of removing subjects, get hold of the depreciation report and the Form B, read what the bylaws say about age restrictions, pets and rentals, and pull the strata minutes covering the past two years. Complexes limited to 55+ or 45+ enforce age bylaws, and those apply to at least one occupant.
Are any Chilliwack condos in the floodplain?

If you're looking at Yarrow, Rosedale, Greendale, lower Sardis or Fairfield Island, ask about flood risk, since parts of those areas are on the Fraser and Vedder Rivers floodplain, behind the City's dike network. Worth asking: what lenders and insurers require, the property's flood construction level, and any geotechnical or floodplain covenant on title.
Which schools serve Chilliwack condos?

School District 33 (SD33) is where Chilliwack belongs. Students from Sardis and the south side go to Sardis Secondary and G.W. Graham. Chilliwack Secondary is the school for the north side. Boundaries get redrawn, so for a particular address check with SD33.
Is public transit available near Chilliwack condos?

Yes. BC Transit's Chilliwack routes include Vedder Road, then Luckakuck Way and Young Road, while the Fraser Valley Express goes on to Abbotsford and Langley. There is little or no bus service in rural parts such as Ryder Lake, Columbia Valley and Greendale.
